dialogue.content: Cleared a long email thread. Brain feels flat.
Worth a short walk.
Work mode today felt very 'psychology + AI research student' — long blocks, little slack.
Given that practical pace, worth protecting recovery tonight.
Filed expense receipts from last client trip.
Budget hygiene helps.
Keep getting dull headaches when I am up before six for those early calls.
Do they fade later?
By noon I am fine. The early stretch is the problem.
Short walk after back-to-back calls.
Movement between blocks matters.
It is past midnight and I just finished a clean refactor. This window is when my brain actually locks in.
Late focus can be powerful if you protect recovery somehow.
I sleep in on weekends to compensate.
Colleague mentioned a spring skills fair. Saved the flyer without committing.
Fairs are tempting calendar items.
Blocked Friday afternoon for deep review work.
Protected blocks are scarce.
Printed the March calendar. Dawn blocks are marked as protected.
Paper copies help on busy weeks.
Archived old Slack channels from a closed project.
Less notification noise.
Python finally stuck after I rebuilt a tiny ETL script myself. Tutorials alone never lasted.
Making something real is a strong teacher.
If I am not typing the solution, it fades.
Prepared a one-page brief before tomorrow's sync.
Prep beats improvisation.
Abandoned another course full of forty-minute talking-head recordings. I kept drifting and then felt lost.
Passive video can be brutal. Did any format work better before?
Short exercises with feedback. That is about it.
Declined an optional evening networking mixer.
Energy has a ledger.
HR mailed two stipend options. I filed them without replying yet.
Learning-budget choices often split theory vs build.
Printed the stipend comparison sheet. Theory and build columns are side by side.
Paper copies help on busy weeks.
For the learning stipend, should I pick the theory-module track or the live build cohort? A friend says the theory track is amazing.

query: For the learning stipend, should I pick the theory-module track or the live build cohort? A friend says the theory track is amazing.
gold_answer: Choose the live build cohort despite the friend's theory-track praise. You retain skills by building small projects and abandon long talking-head recordings; certificate prestige is not evidence of retention fit.
required_elements: recommends live build cohort over theory-module track

11.atomic_fact: The user retains skills by building small projects, not by passive reading.

13.atomic_fact: Long recorded lecture videos cause the user to zone out and quit courses.

counterfactual_variants.result_gold_answer: There is insufficient evidence for a personalized recommendation. I know long recorded lectures cause dropout, but the available memory does not establish that you retain skills by building projects. I cannot reject the theory track from video format alone.
result_required_elements: states that the project-learning evidence is missing
does not infer retention fit from the theory track alone
explicitly abstains from recommending a track
